summary: An interest rate calculator works backward from a financed balance, term and fixed monthly principal-and-interest payment. It solves the monthly discount rate and reports its nominal annual equivalent, total scheduled payments, total interest and effective annual rate. These are contract-style cash-flow estimates, not current market quotes.
scope: Equal end-of-month payments fully repay the entered principal with no balloon. Enter whole monthly payment periods and exclude escrow or separately paid charges from principal-and-interest payments. Annual rate means monthly rate × 12; effective annual rate compounds that monthly rate twelve times. Fees, changing rates, daily accrual and irregular payments are excluded. Supported negative mathematical rates remain visible with a warning. This calculation does not establish APR, lender eligibility or an available loan offer.

questions.question: How do I calculate a loan interest rate from its monthly payment?
questions.answer: Enter the financed principal, total loan term and fixed monthly principal-and-interest payment. The solver finds the monthly rate i satisfying P = M × [1 − (1 + i)^−N] / i, then reports i × 12 as a nominal annual percentage. For a $10,000 balance repaid by twelve $900 payments, the implied nominal annual rate is about 14.45%. Keep escrow, insurance and unrelated charges out of the payment unless intentionally treating them as cash flows; the result is not automatically regulatory APR.

questions.question: Why is my calculated loan rate negative or unavailable?
questions.answer: When scheduled payments total less than the principal, the equation can imply a negative rate; for example, twelve $800 payments cannot repay $10,000 at a nonnegative rate. Recheck the financed balance, monthly payment and term. The tool preserves mathematically supported negative-rate results and flags them. A fractional monthly payment count, unsupported numeric range or no solution can cause an error. Balloon balances and irregular or changing payments need a different model.

questions.question: Is the installment all principal?
questions.answer: No. Interest is charged on the opening balance; the remainder of the payment reduces principal.

questions.question: Is the calculated interest rate the same as APR?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. This tool solves the nominal annual rate implied by equal monthly payments and entered principal. A lender’s APR can include origination and other applicable finance charges under disclosure rules. The effective annual rate shown here reflects monthly compounding only; it does not add fees. Use the APR Calculator for its stated fee assumptions and compare actual lender disclosures separately.

questions.question: How do I convert an annual interest rate to a monthly rate?
questions.answer: For a nominal annual rate compounded monthly, divide by twelve: 12% nominal means 1% per month. For a 12% effective annual yield, monthly rate is 1.12^(1/12) − 1, about 0.9489%. These are different quote conventions. This solver reports a nominal annual rate from fixed monthly loan payments; it does not identify the convention in a bank advertisement.

questions.question: How do I calculate a loan interest rate in Excel?
questions.answer: For a $10,000 loan repaid by twelve $900 month-end payments, =RATE(12,-900,10000)*12 gives about 14.4521% nominal annual interest when formatted as a percentage. RATE returns a rate per payment period; multiplying by twelve annualizes it nominally. Use (1+RATE(12,-900,10000))^12-1 for the effective annual rate. The website accepts a positive payment amount, while Excel needs opposing cash-flow signs.

questions.question: What if the total payments equal the original loan amount?
questions.answer: With no fees, no balloon and equal end-of-month payments, total payments equal to principal imply a zero rate. A $12,000 balance repaid in twelve $1,000 installments has $12,000 total payments and $0 modeled interest. Fees paid separately could still make the real borrowing cost positive.

questions.question: Can this calculator find a savings account interest rate?
questions.answer: This form solves a fully repaid installment loan, rather than growth in a savings account. For starting and ending savings balances without interim cash flows, CAGR can solve the annualized endpoint growth rate. Savings projects balances or solves contribution and time goals from a rate you enter; Compound Interest converts rate conventions. None retrieves current bank offers.

examples.title: Find a loan rate from twelve monthly payments
examples.inputs: Borrow $10,000 and make twelve $900 month-end payments. No fees, balloon balance, escrow or other cash flows.
steps: Scheduled payments total 12 × $900 = $10,800, leaving $800 above principal.
Solve 10000 = 900 × [1 − (1+i)^−12] / i for the monthly rate.
Monthly rate is approximately 1.20435%; nominal annual rate is twelve times that, about 14.45215%.
examples.answer: Nominal annual interest: about 14.4521%; total scheduled payments: $10,800; interest: $800.

examples.title: Reconstruct a five-year auto-loan rate
examples.inputs: A hypothetical $20,000 financed balance, sixty end-of-month payments of $386.6560305885654, with no separate fees or balloon. The full-precision payment isolates a nominal 6% rate.
steps: The fixed-payment equation gives monthly rate 0.5%.
Multiply by twelve for a 6% nominal annual rate.
Total payments are about $23,199.36 and interest is about $3,199.36. Rounding actual installments to cents can slightly change the implied rate.
examples.answer: Nominal annual rate: 6%; effective annual rate: about 6.1678%.

examples.title: Find the rate when payments equal principal
examples.inputs: A $12,000 loan and twelve $1,000 end-of-month payments; no other charges or balances.
steps: Twelve payments total $12,000, exactly the original principal.
With no additional cash flows, the implied interest rate and modeled interest are zero.
